---
title: "Getting started"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = FALSE)
```

```{r}
library(dataeuropa)
```

## Search

`de_search_datasets()` returns a data frame with one row per dataset, with the title and
description in your chosen language (falling back to English, then any available language).

```{r}
df <- de_search_datasets("air quality", country = "de", format = "CSV", limit = 20, lang = "de")
attr(df, "count")        # total hits, not just the rows returned
```

Filters: `country` (ISO-2, e.g. `"pt"`), `catalog`, `format` (`"CSV"`), `license`,
`category` (DCAT-AP theme, e.g. `"ENVI"`), `publisher`, `keywords`, `hvd` (high-value datasets),
plus `sort`, `min_date` / `max_date` / `date_type` and `bbox`.
Values within one filter are OR-ed; different filters are AND-ed:

```{r}
de_search_datasets("budget", country = c("pt", "es"), format = "CSV")   # (PT or ES) and CSV
```

## Searching by area

```{r}
de_search_datasets("rivers", bbox = c(20, 59.7, 31.6, 70.1))   # min lon, min lat, max lon, max lat
```

A dataset matches when its spatial extent overlaps the box, so datasets that cover all of
Europe or the world match any box. Datasets without a spatial extent never match: that is
about half the portal, including whole national catalogues (none of Portugal's 21,000 datasets
has one). Combine `bbox` with `country` with care.

## Counting and facets

```{r}
de_count("flood", country = "nl")            # hits only, no records transferred
de_facet_values("format", q = "flood")       # which formats exist, with counts
de_facet_values("country", top = 10)
```

## More than 1,000 results

The Search API returns at most 1,000 records per request. `de_fetch_datasets()` pages through
larger result sets with the scroll API:

```{r}
df <- de_fetch_datasets("energy", country = "fr", max_results = 5000)
```

## Getting the data

```{r}
dist <- de_distributions(dataset_id)         # files and services of one dataset
path <- de_download(dist[1, ], "data/")
```

Not every distribution is a file. Many are services (WMS, WFS, INSPIRE download services),
and some publisher URLs are placeholders such as `https://localhost/...`.
The `kind` column sorts them: `file`, `service`, `page` (a web page), `none` (no usable URL)
or `unknown`. `de_distributions(dataset_id, files_only = TRUE)` keeps only files.

When the portal lists a checksum for the file (the `checksum` and `checksum_algorithm`
columns; MD5, SHA-1 or SHA-256), the download is checked against it. A mismatch deletes the
file and raises an error; `verify = FALSE` skips the check. Only about 3% of distributions
have a checksum. `byte_size` is not checked, because it is often a placeholder (0, 1, 1024).

## Reading a file into a table

```{r}
dist <- de_distributions(dataset_id)
df <- de_load_distribution(dist[1, ])                    # format detected from the row
df <- de_load_distribution(url, format = "csv")          # or say which
df <- de_load_distribution(url, sheet = "Data")          # XLSX sheet by name or 1-based index
```

Reads CSV and JSON; XLSX with the readxl package and Parquet with the arrow package (both
optional: `install.packages(c("readxl", "arrow"))`). The format comes from the row's format id,
then its media type, then the URL's file extension.

- **CSV**: the delimiter (`,` `;` tab `|`) is detected from the header line; text is read as
  UTF-8, falling back to Latin-1; only empty cells count as missing. Decimal commas (`12,5`) and
  dates stay text.
- **JSON**: an array of objects, or an object holding exactly one such array.

It refuses, with a clear error, services (WMS, WFS, APIs), compressed archives (use
`de_download()` and unpack them), and HTML pages that some publishers serve instead of the file.

## Reading geodata

```r
dist <- de_distributions(dataset_id, files_only = TRUE)
df <- de_load_geodata(dist[1, ])                          # GeoJSON, zipped Shapefile, GeoPackage, KML, GML, ...
df <- de_load_geodata(url, layer = "wells")               # a layer of a GeoPackage, or a file in a ZIP
df <- de_load_geodata(url, crs = "EPSG:4326")             # reproject
df <- de_load_geodata(url, max_mb = Inf)                  # files over 200 MB are refused by default
```

Needs the sf package; GDAL does the reading, so any vector format it knows works. The result is
an sf data frame whose geometry column is `geometry`.

- **ZIP archives** (how shapefiles are published) are opened in place. Inside, the one geodata
  file is read; if there are several, `layer` picks one by file name, otherwise the error lists
  them.
- **Layers**: `layer` picks one by name or 1-based position; by default the first, with a message
  when there are more.
- **Coordinate systems**: the source CRS is kept; `crs` reprojects. A file without one (a
  shapefile without `.prj`) is read as stored, with a warning.
- **Size**: files over `max_mb` megabytes (default 200) are not downloaded. `de_download()` takes
  the same limit as `max_bytes`.

### Feature services (WFS, OGC API Features)

```r
df <- de_load_geodata(row)                                # a WFS or OGC API Features distribution
df <- de_load_geodata(row, layer = "parcels")             # a feature type or collection
df <- de_load_geodata(row, max_features = Inf)            # all features (default: the first 10,000)
```

`de_load_geodata()` also reads WFS (URLs with `service=WFS`, WFS format ids) and OGC API Features
(collection or landing-page URLs, `OGCFEAT`). GDAL pages through the results; each feature type
or collection is a layer. It reads at most `max_features` features, with a warning when there
are more. Other services (WMS, WMTS: images; INSPIRE Atom feeds) and web pages are refused.

## Metadata as RDF, and SPARQL

```{r}
ttl <- de_get_rdf(dataset_id)                 # Turtle; fmt = "jsonld" for JSON-LD
de_sparql("
  SELECT ?format (COUNT(*) AS ?n) WHERE {
    ?d a <http://www.w3.org/ns/dcat#Distribution> ; <http://purl.org/dc/terms/format> ?format
  } GROUP BY ?format ORDER BY DESC(?n) LIMIT 10
")
```

SPARQL queries that filter text across the whole graph can take 10 to 40 seconds.
Always use `LIMIT`.

## Caching responses

```{r}
de_cache_on()                                  # this session; or set DATAEUROPA_CACHE=1
de_cache_on("cache/", ttl = 3600)
de_cache_off()
de_clear_cache()                               # delete cached responses
```

The cache is off by default. When on, it keeps dataset records, the catalogue list, and
searches with `limit` 0 (facet values and counts) on disk for a day, so repeated lookups do not
go back to the portal. Searches that return records, SPARQL and file downloads are never cached.

## Interrupted downloads

Files are written as `<file>.part` and renamed when complete. Calling `de_download()` again with the
same URL and destination continues an interrupted download where it stopped, when the server
supports it (most file hosts do). A file that changed on the server meanwhile is downloaded again
from the start. `resume = FALSE` always starts from the start.

## Settings

| Environment variable | Default | Effect |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `DATAEUROPA_TIMEOUT` | `60` | request timeout in seconds |
| `DATAEUROPA_CACHE` | off | `1` turns the response cache on |
| `DATAEUROPA_CACHE_DIR` | `tools::R_user_dir("dataeuropa", "cache")` | where cached responses go |
| `DATAEUROPA_CACHE_TTL` | `86400` (one day) | how long a cached response stays valid, in seconds |

Requests that fail with HTTP 429 or 5xx are retried with backoff.
